clue.text: Sticky stuff — deuterium and lead — could produce a medal

parts.note: goo is a sticky substance
D is the chemical symbol for deuterium
to lead an orchestra is to conduct it

explanation.surface: A chemistry recipe of glue, heavy hydrogen and lead somehow yields a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer completes the name of the Good Conduct Medal, awarded to service personnel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Good Conduct Medal is a military award, so this behaviour is what earns that decoration.

clue.text: Go belonging to one who belongs to it?

definitions.text: Go belonging to one who belongs to it?

parts.words: Go belonging to one who belongs to it?
parts.note: in this puzzle 'Go' names an implement for striking a ball on the links; the one you carry is owned by a member of the same-named institution

explanation.surface: A riddle about something owned by a member of the body it is named for.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue sets the puzzle's theme: every later 'Go' stands for this answer, so CLEEK, NIBLICK, MASHIE and the rest are all old or modern names of such implements.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the stick swung on a course and the society whose members play there.

clue.text: Explosion, but managed in the FT way

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the street abbreviation phrase

parts.note: the paper speaking of its own road would say 'our street', abbreviated OUR ST

indicators.note: managed means the letters of but are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper's eruption, but handled in its own house style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' turns BUT into TBU, which goes 'in' OUR ST, the FT's 'way' in its own voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden burst of anger or noise is a kind of eruption.

clue.text: Go with cold vegetable

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps
a leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: Someone sets off with a chilled vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the puzzle's shorthand for the theme answer at 1 Down; the answer is an old iron-headed club.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Scottish iron with a narrow face, one of the theme's golfing implements.

clue.text: Go means putting pen to tongue

parts.note: the nib is the writing point of a pen, standing for the whole
a lick is what a tongue gives

explanation.surface: Moving forward means touching a pen to one's tongue, as old writers did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... to' simply sets the pen piece before the tongue piece. 'Go' stands for the 1 Down theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An old lofted iron, roughly a modern nine-iron, so one of the theme's golfing implements.

clue.text: On a high and tipsy but still repressed?

parts.note: to be up is to be elated, on a high
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone elated and merry yet still buttoned-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and inhibited people are described as unable to relax, which is the same idea.

clue.text: Apostles with tables of Roman law

explanation.surface: The disciples paired with an ancient legal code.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twelve Tables were the earliest codified Roman laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ's disciples are called by their number, and the early Roman code is known as its twelve tables.

clue.text: Politician keeping nothing from cleaner

indicators.note: keeping means the politician's letters hold the zero inside

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A politician withholding nothing from a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge on a stick for washing floors is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Temperamental Pole coming in with lament

indicators.note: coming in shows the pole letter entering the temperamental word

parts.note: temperamental means moody
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A moody Polish person arrives with a sad song.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful poem or song for one voice is an elegy, a kind of lament.

clue.text: Go may get shot

explanation.surface: A departure may end in gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' stands for the 1 Down theme; the second sense is one who puts the shot in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-faced club used on the green, and also an athlete who throws the shot, a shot-putter.

clue.text: Turner something of a radical at heart?

indicators.note: something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is the painter Turner a bit of a radical at heart?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' tempts as the painter; it is a machine that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that spins wood or metal for shaping is a turning tool.

clue.text: Space traveller and bird fly around? I don't recommend it

indicators.note: around puts the fly's letters about the other two pieces

parts.note: a bot is a botfly
ET is the film's extraterrestrial
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An alien and a bird flying about earn a disapproving warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Advising someone it would be unwise to act is a way of discouraging it.

clue.text: Little sweetheart's laughter?

parts.note: chuck is a northern English endearment, like love
-ling is a diminutive ending, as in duckling

explanation.surface: A tiny darling giggling.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in reverse of the clue order: CHUCK then the diminutive LING, making a 'little chuck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet suppressed laughing is a kind of mirth.

clue.text: Go on the West Side?

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
an edge is a side

explanation.surface: Heading off to the West Side, as in the musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' stands for the 1 Down theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavily lofted iron for chipping out of sand, part of the theme's golfing kit.

clue.text: Remove plaster from cut skin?

parts.note: peeling an adhesive dressing off a wound means freeing what is stuck

explanation.surface: First-aid advice about taking a dressing off a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeing something adhered, like a dressing pulled away, is detaching it.

clue.text: Go is OK in the foundry

parts.note: Go stands for the theme answer; an iron is one
something that works is OK

explanation.surface: Things are going fine at the foundry.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'Go' gives a piece, not the definition: an iron is one of the theme's implements.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory where iron is smelted and cast is a foundry.

clue.text: Archer to produce story

explanation.surface: A bowman told to come up with a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss legendary bowman bears this name, and narrating a tale is recounting it.

clue.text: Stirrer takes meal at Go

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain
Go stands for the theme; a spoon was an old wooden-headed club

explanation.surface: A troublemaker has a meal while playing the board game Go.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon is used for stirring tea, so it is literally a stirring utensil.

clue.text: Summary: relative of horse turns up

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue says the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: sis is short for sister
of horse is the possessive, pony's

explanation.surface: A summary: a cousin of the horse appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses SIS + PONYS as a whole, giving SYNOP then SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline giving the main points is a short summary.

clue.text: Become quiet? I'm amazed!

parts.note: to go is to become, as in go mad
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Turning silent? How astonishing!
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation of surprise, like goodness.

clue.text: Female holds a very loud note opening Mozart symphony

indicators.note: holds says the female word encloses the rest

parts.note: her refers to a woman
ff is fortissimo, very loud in music

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of note

explanation.surface: A woman sustains a loud note at the start of a Mozart symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 35 is named after the Haffner family of Salzburg.

clue.text: By grasping right container drink can be got here

indicators.note: grasping means the word by holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: taken as written
an ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A drink you can get by holding the right container.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is made at this place, so drink can be obtained there.

clue.text: Go that is after money

indicators.note: after puts the that-is abbreviation behind the money piece

parts.note: brass is northern slang for money
ie abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone chasing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' stands for the 1 Down theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An old brass-soled wooden club, roughly a two-wood, one of the theme's golfing implements.

clue.text: Parents run Go

parts.note: mas are mothers, parents
hie means hurry, run

explanation.surface: Parents operate the board game Go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' stands for the 1 Down theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An old iron for medium approach shots, one of the theme's golfing implements.

clue.text: Go needs a licence

explanation.surface: Setting off requires official permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' stands for the 1 Down theme; the second sense is a motorist, who must hold a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: The club for tee shots, and a motorist, someone who must be licensed.

clue.text: Missile ill associated with school?

indicators.note: ill associated suggests the school's name poorly said, its first letter dropped as in Cockney

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A projectile wrongly linked to a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is an elite English boarding school; said with the aitch dropped it becomes the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed shaft shot from a bow is a projectile weapon.

clue.text: Californian saint in reduced circumstances of an organisation

definitions.text: Californian saint in reduced circumstances of an organisation

parts.words: Californian saint in reduced circumstances of an organisation
parts.note: the patron of a Californian city, given with company shortened to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A saint from California finds himself in a firm's straitened times.
explanation.walkthrough: The Californian city is named for Saint Francis; adding CO, company in 'reduced' form, completes the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish form of the name of the saint for whom the Californian city is named.

clue.text: Conservative is in the red where boats are raced

parts.note: someone in debt owes money

explanation.surface: A Tory is in debt at a sailing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a town on the Isle of Wight, home of Cowes Week sailing regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Wight town hosts a famous annual yachting regatta.

clue.text: Vacillations in London borough (South)

parts.note: Havering is a borough in east London
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Indecision in a south London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithering and wavering are acts of indecision, which is what vacillating is.

clue.text: GCs for the "Master of the Tiger"?

explanation.surface: Golf clubs owned by the famous golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: GCs is golf clubs; Tiger Woods has won the Masters several times.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden-headed clubs form a class of golf clubs, and the golfer Tiger shares this surname.

clue.text: Spike in the side of the head

definitions.text: in the side of the head

explanation.surface: Something sharp lodged in the side of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike of grain on a cereal plant, and the hearing organ on the head's flank.

clue.text: Sapper in hat with goods from Edith Sitwell's work

indicators.note: in puts the sapper inside the hat

parts.note: a Stetson is a cowboy hat
RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers
G is good, so GS is goods

explanation.surface: A soldier in a cowboy hat carrying goods from a poet's collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Street Songs is a 1942 collection of poems by Edith Sitwell.
